intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader jailed for 200 years
items.text: A court in Kenya has sentenced Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a doomsday cult, to 200 years in prison. He was convicted of murdering 191 people, 190 children and one adult. Reports say his followers were moved to a remote area and ordered to fast until they died, and that guards made sure they obeyed. Police later exhumed more than 400 bodies from mass graves. The sentence was announced on Thursday.

gloss.doomsday cult: a religious group that believes the world will end soon
gloss.sentence: to officially decide a punishment for a crime
gloss.convict: to decide in court that someone is guilty
gloss.fast: to eat nothing for a period of time
gloss.exhume: to dig up a dead body from the ground
gloss.mass grave: a large hole where many bodies are buried together

items.title: Herzog to name Israel's next government leader
items.text: Israel's president, Isaac Herzog, says he will announce on Sunday whom he has asked to form the next government. The former military chief Gadi Eisenkot appears to be the favourite. He has been endorsed by 67 members of the Knesset, Israel's parliament, while the current prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has the support of 46. The person Herzog chooses will then try to build a government that can win the support of parliament.

gloss.form a government: to bring together enough politicians to run a country
gloss.favourite: the person most likely to win
gloss.endorse: to say publicly that you support someone
gloss.incumbent: the person who currently holds a job or position

items.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape
items.text: A jury at Southwark Crown Court in London has convicted the comedian Russell Brand, 51, of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was cleared of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault, and he had denied all the allegations. The charges covered incidents between 1999 and 2009, and six women gave evidence. The judge, Joel Bennathan, said Brand will be sentenced on Monday and faces a long prison term. He was taken into custody after the verdict.

gloss.jury: a group of ordinary people who decide if someone is guilty in court
gloss.count: one separate charge in a trial
gloss.clear of: to decide that someone is not guilty of a crime
gloss.allegation: a claim that someone did something wrong, not yet proved
gloss.take into custody: to arrest someone and keep them under police control
gloss.verdict: the final decision of a court or jury

items.title: Alcaraz saves two match points in Paris
items.text: Carlos Alcaraz beat Taylor Fritz 6-7, 7-5, 6-3 in the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters on Friday. The Spaniard saved two match points and came back from a break down in the third set. It is the first time he has reached the semi-finals in Paris. He said it was "one of the most special matches that I ever played". Alcaraz will now play Casper Ruud, who beat Nuno Borges, while Ben Shelton meets Luca Van Assche in the other semi-final.

gloss.match point: a point which, if won, ends the match
gloss.quarter-final: a game in the round with eight players left
gloss.break: winning a game when your opponent is serving
gloss.come back from: to recover from a bad position and do better
gloss.semi-final: a game in the round with four players left

items.title: Protesters storm Microsoft data centre site
items.text: Protesters broke into the construction site of a new Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Thursday. A spokesman for the group Push Back, Nathan Timmer, said: "We don't want it to be built. Nobody needs it." The protesters were clashing with police as the report was published. A data centre is a large building full of computers that store and process information for companies and websites. Euronews also showed the protest in a video report.

gloss.data centre: a building full of computers that store and process information
gloss.construction site: a place where a building is being built
gloss.break into: to enter a place by force without permission
gloss.clash with: to fight or argue with someone
gloss.spokesman: a man who speaks officially for a group

items.title: Scientists give old wind turbine blades a new life
items.text: Researchers have found a way to reuse wind turbine blades, which are hard to recycle. In a study in the journal Chem Circularity, they heated old blades to about 2,000 degrees Celsius for a few seconds. The blades turned into silicon carbide and graphene. Adding just 0.3 per cent of this material to resin made it stronger and stiffer. Euronews says the amount of blade waste in Europe could rise from 20,000 tonnes in 2025 to 55,000 tonnes by 2030.

gloss.turbine: a machine with blades that turns wind into electricity
gloss.resin: a sticky substance that becomes hard and is used to make plastics
gloss.upcycle: to reuse something to make a product that is better than the original
gloss.landfill: a place where rubbish is buried in the ground
gloss.hard to recycle: difficult to process so that the material can be used again

items.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production
items.text: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory next year, Elon Musk has said. Reuters reports that the decision follows years of poor sales in a small number of markets. The Cybertruck is an electric pickup truck made by Tesla. Euronews also reported the news in a video bulletin on Friday, saying Tesla would "wind down" production of the vehicle next year.

gloss.wind down: to reduce an activity slowly until it stops
gloss.pickup truck: a vehicle with an open area at the back for carrying things
gloss.gigafactory: the name Tesla uses for its very large factories
gloss.poor sales: when few people buy a product
gloss.market: a country or area where a product is sold

items.title: Europeans may need to save more for retirement
items.text: The OECD says mandatory pensions in 22 of 30 European countries studied will not reach its target of 70 per cent of gross pay. The extra share of earnings people need to save is called the contribution gap. For a man on an average wage it is 9.1 per cent in the UK, 6.2 per cent in France and 11.1 per cent in Germany. In Lithuania it is the highest, at 20.7 per cent. In the UK, that means about 494 euros more a month.

gloss.gross pay: the amount you earn before tax is taken off
gloss.contribution: money paid regularly into a pension
gloss.gap: a difference between what exists and what is needed
gloss.retirement: the time of life when you stop working

items.title: Rockstar shows GTA VI launch gallery
items.text: Rockstar Games has published a launch gallery for Grand Theft Auto VI on its website. The company said on Thursday that the game is now officially only two weeks away. It added: "See you in Leonida on November 19." The game will come out on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. Tech Insider reports that Rockstar gave no price or story details with the gallery, and that digital pre-loading starts on 10 November.

gloss.gallery: a collection of pictures shown together
gloss.launch: the day a new product is first sold
gloss.pre-load: to download a game before it is released
gloss.come out: to be released for people to buy
gloss.officially: in a way that is announced by the people in charge

items.title: US states vote on girls' sport
items.text: Voters in two US states have backed rules that would limit girls' and women's sport to people who are female. Colorado's Proposition 134 and Washington's Measure 638 both passed in referendums this week. The rules are based on sex rather than gender. The Morning Star notes that both states usually vote for the Democratic Party. A referendum is a vote in which people decide a single question directly, instead of electing a politician to decide.

gloss.referendum: a public vote on one question
gloss.measure: a proposed law that voters decide on
gloss.endorse: to say publicly that you support something
gloss.limit to: to allow only a certain group
